test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 05 Feb, 2026 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: A man borrowed Rs. 18,000 at 10\% per annum simple interest. After 3 years, he repaid the borrowed money along with the interest by giving a motorcycle worth 12,000 and the remaining in cash. Find the amount of cash he paid.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective Simple Interest rate for 3 years = 10% × 3 = 30%

Total Payable Amount = 130% of 18,000 = ₹23,400

Cash to be paid = Total Amount − Motorcycle value

Cash = 23,400 − 12,000 = ₹11,400

**∴ The correct answer is ₹11,400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹18,000

Rate (R) = 10% per annum

Time (T) = 3 years

Value of Motorcycle = ₹12,000

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Total Amount (A) = Principal + SI

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9458fad0eca0b08bc850d19409b2d43367dc9c4e7a22bdc066c31e46cf6a5a28.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI = (18,000 × 10 × 3) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 180 × 30

⇒ SI = ₹5,400

⇒ Total Amount = 18,000 + 5,400

⇒ Total Amount = ₹23,400

⇒ Cash Paid = Total Amount − Motorcycle Value

⇒ Cash Paid = 23,400 − 12,000

⇒ Cash Paid = ₹11,400

**∴ The correct answer is ₹11,400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

For the first year, SI and CI are always equal if the interest is compounded annually on the same principal and rate.

Effective Rate of Interest

The effective rate for simple interest over 'T' years is (R ×T)%. In this case, 10 × 3 = 30%.

Total Amount Formula

Amount can also be calculated as A = P(1 + RT/100). Here, A = 18000(1 + 30/100) = 18000 × 1.3 = ₹23,400.
